sampling_model.design: Population equality of full positive-definite covariance models is the identification kernel; the statistical rung uses independent Gaussian sampling and global BIC over the finite labelled state class.
sampling_model.units: Each observation is one independent realization of the \(p\)-variable centered linear Gaussian SEM.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment in the structure-identification theorem; the prespecified pairs in \(\mathcal Q\) index downstream interventions and responses.
sampling_model.overlap: Not applicable; every innovation variance is positive and otherwise unrestricted.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: For each candidate state and positive-definite sample covariance, target-local block-incidence matrices define positive-definite Gram systems whose unique solutions estimate the common coefficient in each parent block; strictly positive constrained residual variances estimate the innovation variances. The effect maps apply these same off-model block-constrained solutions before taking finite path sums and derivatives. A deterministic measurable fallback invokes no Gram inverse, likelihood supremum, or derivative when \(S_n\) is singular, and all asymptotic claims run through integers \(n\geq p\).

tldr: Equal incoming coefficients encode communities of direct causes. The published blocked edge-coloured class permits singleton blocks, whereas BPEC is its proper no-singleton subclass and is structurally identifiable. On the full singleton-permitting blocked class, equality of the full positive-definite covariance models is characterized exactly by common skeleton and unshielded colliders, common repeated parent blocks, and fixed orientation across unequal endpoint block families; equivalently, the states are connected by partition-compatible singleton covered reversals. The static class is also the set of consistent extensions of the ordinary CPDAG after inserting the background arrows \(F(C)\), with one canonical partition lift per extension. This yields exact-once enumeration after \(O(p^3)\) initialization and \(O(p+m)\) delay, a sharp \(p!\) component bound, generic fixed-\(p\) BIC component recovery, and simultaneous inference for the finite effect set. Deterministic output-sensitive quotienting by global rational identity of compact effect circuits remains open.

project_justification.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves BPEC structural identifiability only after forbidding singleton edge-colour classes and explicitly leaves graphical and transformational edge-coloured equivalence open. Ordinary covered reversals ignore coefficient partitions, while partial homoscedasticity constrains innovation variances rather than incoming coefficients.
project_justification.niche: Target-local blocked colourings with unrestricted positive noise variances form a natural intermediate class: repeated blocks reveal stable causal communities, but singleton blocks retain exactly the ordinary orientation ambiguity compatible with those communities.
project_justification.fill: The project recovers repeated blocks from the identity tangent space, proves by an exact sparse regression separator that any reversed edge must join equal endpoint families, and combines these facts with monotone covered reversals to obtain the full static and transformational characterization. It then converts the static class to a canonical background PDAG: every repeated-block arrow is in \(F(C)\), every consistent extension has a unique path-independent partition lift, and the published linear-delay PDAG enumeration algorithm therefore enumerates the blocked component exactly once. The same quotient supports generic fixed-dimensional BIC recovery and simultaneous possible-effect inference, while exact output-sensitive rational-functional quotienting is isolated as a separate arithmetic-circuit problem.

related_work: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 is the writing and primary method anchor. Its Definition 5.14 defines blocked edge colourings without excluding singleton classes; properness is a separate condition, and BPEC is the blocked, proper no-singleton subclass. Its Theorem 5.17 proves structural identifiability within BPEC, while Question 5.19 asks for a graphical characterization of edge-coloured model equivalence. The present result agrees with that boundary on the BPEC subclass and gives a complete equivalence characterization on the published blocked superclass; it does not transfer a BPEC converse to arbitrary cross-target colourings. Chickering1995 supplies the disagreement-decreasing sequence of distinct covered reversals, while the tangent and separator arguments prove those reversals are legal for the coefficient partitions. WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023, Theorem 5, is used directly after forming the CPDAG-plus-\(F(C)\) PDAG: cubic Meek-closure initialization and linear-delay enumeration of consistent extensions carry over through the newly proved canonical partition-lift bijection. WienobstBannachLiskiewicz2023 addresses counting and sampling ordinary Markov classes, not rational effect-map quotienting. WuDrton2023 constrains innovation variances rather than incoming coefficients, and MakamReichenbachSeigal2023 studies likelihood geometry for a fixed compatibly coloured graph. Haughton1988 informs the finite smooth-model BIC argument. MaathuisKalischBuhlmann2009, ChangGuoMalinsky2026, and GuoPerkovic2022EfficientLS inform possible-effect estimation and inference but do not provide simultaneous inference over this full-model-equivalence component.
technical_internal_limitation: The population component \(\mathcal R(C)\) is an equivalence class of complete covariance-model images, not the pointwise fibre of every state fitting one exceptional covariance. Zero edges and coincident coefficients can create additional pointwise representations outside the component. The fixed directed set \(F(C)\) records orientations forced directly by unequal nonsingleton families, while ordinary collider, acyclicity, and Meek-closure constraints can compel further arrows; neither kind of compelled arrow alone identifies a numerical coefficient. Canonical PDAG enumeration is linear-delay in state outputs, but the number of distinct rational effect maps can be much smaller than the number of states. Exact global rational identity is decidable by denominator clearing and coefficient expansion, yet no deterministic output-polynomial or polynomial-delay canonicalization bound for compact arithmetic circuits is claimed.
honest_scope: The equivalence theorem concerns finite labelled causally sufficient linear Gaussian DAGs, target-local coefficient blocks, unrestricted real block coefficients, unrestricted positive target-specific innovation variances, and full positive-definite covariance images. It does not cover cross-target edge colours, vertex-coloured innovation variances, latent confounding, selection, cycles, or pointwise supermodel fibres. State enumeration uses the canonical CPDAG-plus-\(F(C)\) PDAG and has \(O(p^3)\) initialization and \(O(p+m)\) delay after output-linear partition lifting; attaching a shortest legal-reversal certificate has the safe bound \(O(p^5)\) per output. The sharp state-count bound is \(p!\), attained by the complete all-singleton state. Exact quotienting of the emitted compact rational effect circuits is finite but not shown output-polynomial. The BIC and confidence results remain fixed-\(p\), pointwise, and generic away from a proper algebraic exceptional set; no greedy-search consistency or uniform inference near model intersections is asserted.
interpretation: Repeated coefficient blocks do two jobs. They survive every observationally equivalent representation, and each of their arrows becomes background knowledge because a parent contained in a repeated block cannot have the same block family as the target. After those arrows are fixed, the remaining graph uncertainty is precisely an ordinary Markov-equivalence extension problem, and the endpoint parent sets determine all residual singleton blocks uniquely. This orientation information is structural: an arrow compelled by the PDAG or by \(F(C)\) does not by itself identify its numerical coefficient.

standard.name: Published blocked target-local edge colouring, with properness not imposed

definitions.name: Published singleton-permitting blocked state class
definitions.construction:
The published blocked edge-coloured superclass, specialized to unrestricted target-specific innovation variances, is
\[
\mathfrak S_p=\left\{A=(\mathcal K,\Xi):\mathcal K\text{ is an acyclic directed graph on }V,\ \Xi_j\text{ is a partition of }\operatorname{pa}_{\mathcal K}(j)\text{ for every }j\in V\right\}.
\]
Singleton blocks are permitted. The BPEC class is the proper subclass in which no edge-colour block is a singleton.

definitions.name: Full blocked covariance model
definitions.construction: For \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\), let \(b_E=\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^E_j|\), \(\Theta_E=\mathbb R^{b_E}\times(0,\infty)^p\), and \[\mathcal M(E)=\left\{(I_p-B_E(\beta_E))^{-1}\operatorname{diag}(\omega_E)(I_p-B_E(\beta_E))^{-\mathsf T}:(\beta_E,\omega_E)\in\Theta_E\right\}.\] Here \(B_E(\beta_E)_{ji}=\beta_{jB}\) for \(i\in B\in\Pi^E_j\), and all real block coefficients are admitted.

definitions.name: Off-diagonal model tangent
definitions.construction: At \(I_p\in\mathcal M(E)\), define \[T_E^{\circ}=\operatorname{proj}_{\mathrm{off}}T_{I_p}\mathcal M(E)=\operatorname{span}\{v_{jB}:j\in V,\ B\in\Pi^E_j\},\qquad \operatorname{supp}(v_{jB})=\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}.\]

definitions.name: Partition-compatible singleton covered reversal
definitions.construction: For \(i\to j\) in \(G_E\), \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}(E)\) is defined exactly when \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(j)=\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(i)\cup\{i\}\), \(\{i\}\in\Pi^E_j\), and \(\Pi^E_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi^E_i\). It reverses \(i\to j\), sets \(\Pi'_j=\Pi^E_i\) and \(\Pi'_i=\Pi^E_i\cup\{\{j\}\}\), and leaves every other partition unchanged.

definitions.name: Legal-reversal component
definitions.construction: \[\mathcal R(E)=\{E'\in\mathfrak S_p:E'\text{ is reached from }E\text{ by a finite sequence of defined }\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\}.\]

definitions.name: Canonical PDAG component enumerator with breadth-first fallback
definitions.construction: Given \(C=(G,\Pi)\), construct the canonical background PDAG \(\mathcal P_C\) from \(\texttt{def:canonical-background-pdag}\), compute its Meek closure, and apply the consistent-extension enumerator of \(\texttt{lem:pdag-consistent-extension-enumeration}\). For every emitted DAG \(H\), emit the canonical state \(\mathsf L_C(H)\) from \(\texttt{def:canonical-partition-lift}\); the emitted set is \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\). The primary procedure is exact-once without state memoization. When a shortest certificate is requested, repeatedly scan for a covered arrow that disagrees with \(H\), reverse it, and canonically lift each intermediate graph. As a simple fallback, initialize a queue and exact visited set with \(C\), apply every defined \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\), append each unvisited state, and stop when the queue is empty.

definitions.name: Off-model target-local block-constrained least-squares map
definitions.construction: Fix \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), and \(j\in V\). Write \(P_{Ej}=\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(j)\), and let \(A_{Ej}\) have rows \(i\in P_{Ej}\), columns \(B\in\Pi^E_j\), and entries \((A_{Ej})_{iB}=\mathbf 1\{i\in B\}\). If \(P_{Ej}\neq\varnothing\), define \[\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)=A_{Ej}^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{P_{Ej},P_{Ej}}A_{Ej},\qquad h_{Ej}(\Sigma)=A_{Ej}^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{P_{Ej},j},\qquad \beta_{Ej}(\Sigma)=\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)^{-1}h_{Ej}(\Sigma).\] The columns of \(A_{Ej}\) are linearly independent because \(\Pi^E_j\) is a partition into nonempty blocks, so \(\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)\) is positive definite and the solution is unique. Set \((L_E(\Sigma))_{ji}=\beta_{Ej,B}(\Sigma)\) for \(i\in B\in\Pi^E_j\) and zero for \(i\notin P_{Ej}\); if \(P_{Ej}=\varnothing\), take the unique empty coefficient vector and set row \(j\) to zero. Thus \(L_E(\Sigma)\) is defined for every \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), is rational in the entries of \(\Sigma\), and is smooth on the positive-definite cone.

definitions.name: Global blocked-state BIC
definitions.construction: For each \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\), set \(d_E=p+\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^E_j|\). On the measurable event \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), compute \(L_E(S_n)\) using the block-design systems in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\). For each target set \(\widehat\omega_{Ej}=S_{n,jj}-h_{Ej}(S_n)^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)^{-1}h_{Ej}(S_n)\), with \(\widehat\omega_{Ej}=S_{n,jj}\) for an empty parent set. Positive definiteness of \(S_n\) makes every nonempty \(\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)\) positive definite and every \(\widehat\omega_{Ej}\) strictly positive, so the Gaussian likelihood supremum is finite and attained and \[\operatorname{BIC}_n(E)=-2\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(E)}\ell_n(\Sigma)+d_E\log n.\] On \(S_n\notin\mathbb S^p_{++}\), invoke no Gram inverse, residual-variance formula, or likelihood supremum and set \(\operatorname{BIC}_n(E)=d_E\log n\). For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), let \(\widehat C_n\) be the minimizer over \(\mathfrak S_p\) selected by a fixed deterministic ordering of states.

definitions.name: Generic component-selection exception
definitions.construction: For \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), let \(\mathcal E_C\subsetneq\Theta_C\) be the finite union, over \(D\in\mathfrak S_p\) with \(d_D\leq d_C\) and \(\mathcal M(D)\neq\mathcal M(C)\), of the polynomial pullbacks of \(\mathcal M(C)\cap\mathcal M(D)\), augmented by the polynomial zero-gradient loci of the reported nonconstant effect coordinates.

definitions.name: Component total-effect set
definitions.construction: For \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\) and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), compute the explicit block-constrained map \(L_D(\Sigma)\) from \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\) for every \(D\in\mathcal R(E)\). Define \(g_D(\Sigma)=(((I_p-L_D(\Sigma))^{-1})_{ya})_{(a,y)\in\mathcal Q}\) and \[\mathcal T_E(\Sigma)=\{g_D(\Sigma):D\in\mathcal R(E)\}.\] Because \(G_D\) is acyclic, \(I_p-L_D(\Sigma)\) is invertible. Each \(g_D\) is rational and smooth on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), and \(\mathrm Dg_D(\Sigma)\) is defined throughout that cone. The causal target is the specialization \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma)\) for \(\Sigma\in\mathcal M(C)\).

definitions.name: Simultaneous component-effect confidence collection
definitions.construction: For every \(n\in\mathbb N\), first select \(\widehat C_n\) by \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\). On \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\), order the finite member-labelled coordinates \(g_E(S_n)\) for \(E\in\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)\), compute every \(L_E(S_n)\) through the block-design Gram system in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\), and evaluate the derivative \(\mathrm Dg_E(S_n)\) of the rational map in \(\texttt{def:component-effect-set}\) only on this open positive-definite domain. Use these derivatives with the plug-in Gaussian sample-covariance covariance matrix to obtain delta-method standard errors. Let \(K\) be the number of nonconstant labelled coordinates. If \(K\geq1\), use critical value \(z_{1-\alpha/(2K)}\) for those coordinates and report structurally zero coordinates as singleton intervals; if \(K=0\), report only the singleton intervals and do not evaluate a critical value. On \(S_n\notin\mathbb S^p_{++}\), invoke no Gram inverse, coefficient map, or delta-method derivative and assign the interval \(\mathbb R\) to every member-labelled coordinate. The resulting total measurable collection is \(\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\).

definitions.name: Canonical-state global-rational quotient handle
definitions.construction: The handle \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\) first runs \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\), whose canonical lift removes all path-dependent partition choices. For each emitted state \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), form a compact rational arithmetic circuit for \(g_E\). Two circuits are declared equivalent only when they define the same rational map on the whole cone \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\): clear their positive block-Gram determinant denominators coordinatewise and produce a deterministic exact polynomial-identity certificate, for example the fully expanded coefficient table. Emit one representative circuit per certified identity class together with the list of all member states and their shortest legal-reversal certificates. Numerical evaluations are never used as identity certificates. This handle names a terminating exact procedure; it does not assert an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay bound in the number of distinct rational maps.

definitions.name: Canonical CPDAG with block-family background arrows
definitions.construction: Let \(\operatorname{CPDAG}(G)\) denote the ordinary completed partially directed acyclic graph whose consistent DAG extensions are the Markov-equivalence class of \(G\). Define \(\mathcal P_C\) by retaining every directed edge of \(\operatorname{CPDAG}(G)\) and, for every adjacency whose orientation belongs to \(F(C)\), inserting that orientation from \(G\); every remaining unoriented adjacency stays undirected. The construction does not require \(\mathcal P_C\) to be maximally oriented; its Meek closure is the corresponding MPDAG with the same consistent extensions.

definitions.name: Canonical partition lift of a DAG extension
definitions.construction:
Fix \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\). For a DAG \(H\) on \(V\) satisfying \(\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j(C)}B\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\) for every \(j\in V\), put
\[
 U_j(C)=\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j(C)}B,
 \qquad
 \Lambda^H_j=\mathcal N_j(C)\cup
 \left\{\{i\}:i\in\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\setminus U_j(C)\right\},
\]
and define the partial canonical lift by \(\mathsf L_C(H)=(H,\Lambda^H)\).

statements.statement: For any \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\), equality \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\) implies equality of their skeletons and \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for every \(j\in V\). More precisely, the inclusion-minimal nonempty supports in \(T_C^{\circ}\) are exactly \(\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}\) for \(B\in\Pi_j\); every support of size at least two has a unique center \(j\) and recovers the labelled block \(B\), while a support of size one recovers only the underlying edge. Thus every edge whose orientation differs between \(G\) and \(H\) is a singleton block in both states.
statements.justification: The tangent support partition is the first orientation-robust observable that distinguishes repeated incoming coefficient blocks from reversible singleton edges.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Theorem 4.1 and Section 5, gives smoothness and fixed-graph rational recovery but no cross-DAG recovery of target-local blocks from equality of model images.
statements.consumer: The lemma lets a covariance-model comparison recover causal communities without knowing which Markov-equivalent orientation generated them.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{lem:blocked-model-geometry}\), \(I_p\) is a smooth point of every blocked model and
\[
 T_C^{\circ}=\operatorname{span}\{v_{jB}:j\in V,\ B\in\Pi_j\},
 \qquad \operatorname{supp}(v_{jB})=\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}.
\]
Every unordered skeleton edge occurs in exactly one such support: it is assigned to the partition block at its unique head, and blocks at a fixed head are disjoint. Hence distinct generators have disjoint supports.

If \(w=\sum_{j,B}a_{jB}v_{jB}\neq0\), disjointness gives
\[
 \operatorname{supp}(w)=\bigcup_{a_{jB}\neq0}\operatorname{supp}(v_{jB});
\]
there is no coordinate cancellation. It follows in both directions that the inclusion-minimal nonempty supports of vectors in \(T_C^{\circ}\) are precisely the individual generator supports. Their union is \(\operatorname{skel}(G)\).

Equality \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\) implies equality of their tangent spaces at their common point \(I_p\), and therefore equality of these support partitions. A support containing at least two distinct edges is a star with a unique common endpoint. That endpoint must be the head \(j\), and the other endpoints recover the labelled block \(B\); these are exactly the members of \(\mathcal N_j(C)\). A one-edge support has no distinguishable endpoint and recovers only its underlying unordered edge. Applying the same argument to \(D\) proves skeleton equality and \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for every \(j\). If an edge reverses, it cannot belong to any recovered nonsingleton block in either state, so it is a singleton block in both.

statements.statement: Let \(C,D\in\mathfrak S_p\) satisfy \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\), and suppose \(x\to y\) is in \(G\) while \(y\to x\) is in \(H\). Then \(\mathcal N_x(C)=\mathcal N_y(C)\). Specifically, if \(S\in\mathcal N_x(C)\) is split across two blocks of \(\Pi_y\), choosing unit innovation variances, coefficient one on \(x\to y\), coefficient one on a block \(T\in\Pi_y\) meeting but not containing \(S\), and zero elsewhere gives a covariance in \(\mathcal M(C)\) whose regression of \(X_x\) on \(\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\) has coefficient \(-q\mathbf 1\{s\in T\}\) on \(s\in S\), with \(q=(2+|T\setminus(\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\setminus\{y\})|)^{-1}>0\), contradicting the block \(S\) in \(D\).
statements.justification: This sparse covariance witness is the load-bearing necessity step because it handles arbitrary extra target parents and simultaneous arrow changes.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Lemma 5.11 and the proof of Theorem 5.17, separates reversals only in the proper-colouring regime; it does not establish the endpoint-family condition when singleton blocks coexist with repeated blocks.
statements.consumer: The separator certifies when a proposed singleton reversal changes the complete covariance model, preventing a learner from merging observationally distinguishable causal-community states.
statements.proof_tex:
By \(\texttt{lem:tangent-block-recovery}\), the edge is singleton in both states and the labelled nonsingleton families agree targetwise between \(C\) and \(D\). By \(\texttt{lem:edge-coloured-model-equivalence-markov}\), \(G\) and \(H\) have the same unshielded colliders.

Fix \(S\in\mathcal N_x(C)\) and \(s\in S\). Tangent recovery gives \(s\to x\) in both graphs. If \(s\) and \(y\) were nonadjacent, then \(s\to x\to y\) in \(G\) would become the unshielded collider \(s\to x\leftarrow y\) in \(H\), impossible. Thus \(s\) and \(y\) are adjacent. The orientation \(y\to s\) in \(G\) would create the directed cycle \(y\to s\to x\to y\), so \(s\to y\). Since \(s\) was arbitrary,
\[
 S\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_G(y).
\]

Suppose that \(S\) is not contained in one block of \(\Pi_y\). Then some \(T\in\Pi_y\) meets but does not contain \(S\). Because \(\{x\}\) is the singleton block containing the reversed edge, \(x\notin T\). In the model for \(C\), set every innovation variance to one, set the coefficients on \(x\to y\) and on the block \(T\) to one, and set all other block coefficients to zero. These are admitted parameter values under \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\). Every variable other than \(X_y\) is then an independent standard Gaussian, while
\[
 X_y=X_x+\sum_{r\in T}X_r+\varepsilon_y.
\]
The resulting covariance is positive definite because it is generated with strictly positive innovation variances.

Let \(P=\operatorname{pa}_H(x)\) and \(Q=P\setminus\{y\}\). The preceding graph argument and targetwise tangent recovery give \(S\subseteq Q\). Residualizing \(X_y\) against \(X_Q\) leaves
\[
 Z=X_x+\sum_{r\in T\setminus Q}X_r+\varepsilon_y,\qquad
 h=\operatorname{Var}(Z)=2+|T\setminus Q|>0.
\]
All displayed summands are mutually independent. Therefore the coefficient on \(X_y\) in the regression of \(X_x\) on \((X_Q,X_y)\) is
\[
 q=\frac{\operatorname{Cov}(X_x,Z)}{\operatorname{Var}(Z)}
 =\frac1{2+|T\setminus Q|}>0.
\]
Before adding \(X_y\), the regression coefficient on every \(X_s\), \(s\in Q\), is zero. The residualization identity therefore gives the final coefficient
\[
 -q\,\mathbf 1\{s\in T\},\qquad s\in S.
\]
Since \(T\cap S\neq\varnothing\) and \(S\nsubseteq T\), these coefficients take both values \(-q\) and \(0\) on \(S\). But \(S\in\mathcal N_x(D)\), so every covariance in \(\mathcal M(D)\) must have equal parent-regression coefficients on \(S\), by the recovery formula in \(\texttt{lem:blocked-model-geometry}\). The constructed covariance lies in \(\mathcal M(C)\setminus\mathcal M(D)\), contradicting model equality. Hence each \(S\in\mathcal N_x(C)\) is contained in a member \(T\in\mathcal N_y(C)\).

Apply the same argument after exchanging \(C,D\) and \(x,y\). Every such \(T\) is contained in a member \(U\in\mathcal N_x(C)\). Thus \(S\subseteq T\subseteq U\). Since \(S\) and \(U\) are intersecting blocks in the same partition at \(x\), they are equal; hence \(S=T=U\). This proves \(\mathcal N_x(C)\subseteq\mathcal N_y(C)\), and symmetry gives the reverse inclusion.

statements.statement: For every \(C=(G,\Pi),D=(H,\Lambda)\in\mathfrak S_p\), the following are equivalent: \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\); \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\), equivalently \(G,H\) have the same skeleton and unshielded colliders, \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) for all \(j\in V\), and every edge joining vertices with unequal nonsingleton families has the same orientation; and \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\). Every step in the final characterization is a partition-compatible singleton covered reversal with the prescribed transport. Moreover, \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D)\), and a shortest path reverses each disagreeing arrow exactly once. When no parent block of \(C\) is a singleton, \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), agreeing with the BPEC structural-identifiability theorem on its proper no-singleton subclass. The preceding equivalence criterion applies to the published blocked superclass that also permits singleton blocks.
statements.justification: The theorem identifies the exact full-model quotient on the published singleton-permitting blocked class and gives both its static recovery functional and its legal local transformation calculus.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026 proves uniqueness only inside the proper no-singleton BPEC subclass and asks for edge-coloured equivalence; Chickering1995 has no coefficient-partition legality condition.
statements.consumer: An extension of the colouredDAGs workflow can report the exact covariance-equivalence component while retaining every repeated-coefficient community.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(C=(G,\Pi)\) and \(D=(H,\Lambda)\) in \(\mathfrak S_p\). By \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\), both graphs are finite labelled DAGs and each displayed family is a partition of the corresponding parent set. By \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\), all block coefficients range over \(\mathbb R\), every innovation variance lies in \((0,\infty)\), and \(\mathcal M(E)\) is the full positive-definite covariance image of the SEM. Thus the causal object to be recovered is the graph--partition state up to \(\mathcal R(C)\), whereas equality of the observable full-model images is the identifying relation to be proved equivalent to it.

Suppose first that
\[
 \mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D).
\]
The result \(\texttt{lem:edge-coloured-model-equivalence-markov}\) gives
\[
 \operatorname{skel}(G)=\operatorname{skel}(H),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{uc}(G)=\operatorname{uc}(H).
\]
The already established tangent-support result \(\texttt{lem:tangent-block-recovery}\) gives, vertex by vertex,
\[
 \mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D),\qquad j\in V.
\]
Consider an adjacency \(\{x,y\}\) whose orientations in \(G\) and \(H\) differ. The already established sparse-separator result \(\texttt{lem:reversed-edge-separator}\) yields
\[
 \mathcal N_x(C)=\mathcal N_y(C).
\]
Taking the contrapositive, every adjacency whose endpoint families are unequal has the same orientation in \(G\) and \(H\). Since the skeleton and the vertex-indexed families agree, the definition \(\texttt{def:family-mismatch-edges}\) therefore gives \(F(C)=F(D)\). All four coordinates in \(\texttt{def:static-signature}\) agree, so
\[
 \mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D).
\]

Conversely, suppose \(\mathsf S(C)=\mathsf S(D)\). Equality of the first two signature coordinates and \(\texttt{lem:verma-pearl-markov-equivalence}\) show that \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent. Put
\[
 \mathcal N_j:=\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D),\qquad j\in V.
\]
By \(\texttt{lem:chickering-monotone-covered-reversals}\), there is a sequence
\[
 G=G_0,G_1,\ldots,G_r=H,
 \qquad r=\delta(C,D),
\]
in which \(G_{t+1}\) is obtained from \(G_t\) by reversing one covered arrow that disagrees with \(H\); the reversed underlying edges are distinct, and every intermediate graph is an acyclic member of the same Markov-equivalence class.

We lift this sequence inductively. Let \(E_t=(G_t,\Pi^t)\) be the current blocked state and assume
\[
 \mathcal N_k(E_t)=\mathcal N_k,\qquad k\in V.
\]
This holds for \(t=0\). Suppose the selected covered arrow is \(i\to j\). It is one of the original arrows on which \(G\) and \(H\) disagree. If \(\mathcal N_i\neq\mathcal N_j\), that arrow belongs to \(F(C)\), and equality \(F(C)=F(D)\) forces the same orientation in \(G\) and \(H\), a contradiction. Hence
\[
 \mathcal N_i=\mathcal N_j=:\mathcal N.
\]
Let \(B\in\Pi^t_j\) be the unique block containing \(i\). If \(|B|\geq2\), then \(B\in\mathcal N_j(E_t)=\mathcal N\). Equality of the endpoint families implies \(B\in\mathcal N_i(E_t)\), and every member of the latter family is a subset of \(\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(i)\). But \(i\in B\), which would make \(i\) its own parent. A DAG has no self-loop, so this is impossible. Therefore
\[
 B=\{i\},
 \qquad \{i\}\in\Pi^t_j.
\]

Coveredness says
\[
 P:=\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(i)
   =\operatorname{pa}_{G_t}(j)\setminus\{i\}.
\]
Let \(U=\bigcup_{A\in\mathcal N}A\). The nonsingleton blocks at \(i\) and \(j\) are exactly \(\mathcal N\). If \(k\in P\setminus U\), the block containing \(k\) in either target partition cannot have size at least two, for then it would belong to \(\mathcal N\) and put \(k\) in \(U\). Thus that block is \(\{k\}\) in both partitions. Consequently
\[
 \Pi^t_i=\mathcal N\cup\bigl\{\{k\}:k\in P\setminus U\bigr\},
\]
and, using the already proved singleton status of \(i\to j\),
\[
 \Pi^t_j=\mathcal N\cup\bigl\{\{k\}:k\in P\setminus U\bigr\}
                 \cup\{\{i\}\}.
\]
Hence
\[
 \Pi^t_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi^t_i.
\]
The three conditions in \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\) now hold. Applying \(\operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}\) gives a state \(E_{t+1}\) with graph \(G_{t+1}\); by \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\), it preserves all nonsingleton families, so the induction continues.

After \(r\) steps the graph is \(H\). A parent set \(P_j\) and a compatible nonsingleton family \(\mathcal N_j\) determine the entire partition uniquely:
\[
 \mathcal N_j\cup
 \left\{\{k\}:k\in P_j\setminus
       \bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j}B\right\}.
\]
The final state and \(D\) have the same graph \(H\) and the same nonsingleton families, so their partitions both equal this display. Thus the final state is \(D\), proving \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\).

If instead \(D\in\mathcal R(C)\), the definition \(\texttt{def:reversal-component}\) supplies a finite legal-reversal sequence from \(C\) to \(D\). Repeated application of \(\texttt{lem:legal-reversal-model-invariance}\) gives equality of the covariance-model image at every step, hence
\[
 \mathcal M(D)=\mathcal M(C).
\]
This proves equivalence of all three criteria.

The lifted Chickering sequence has \(\delta(C,D)\) steps and reverses each disagreeing edge once. Conversely, each legal move reverses only one skeleton edge. Every edge oriented differently in the endpoints must be reversed an odd, hence positive, number of times along any path. Therefore every legal path has length at least \(\delta(C,D)\), and
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D).
\]

It remains to check the proper-block boundary and the edge fact used by the canonical reduction. For any \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) and \(i\in B\), one has \(i\to j\) in \(G\). Equality \(\mathcal N_i(C)=\mathcal N_j(C)\) would imply \(B\in\mathcal N_i(C)\), hence \(i\in\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\), which is impossible. Thus
\[
 B\in\mathcal N_j(C),\ i\in B
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)
 \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 i\to j\in F(C).
\]
If no block is a singleton, every edge is covered by the first premise in this display. Hence every arrow belongs to \(F(C)\) and is fixed by the static criterion. The fixed graph and fixed nonsingleton families determine every partition, so \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\). This is exactly the BPEC conclusion supplied by \(\texttt{lem:bpec-proper-identifiability}\) on the proper no-singleton subclass. The larger class \(\mathfrak S_p\) is the published blocked superclass with singleton blocks admitted; its nontrivial components are characterized by the equivalence just proved, not by transferring the BPEC converse beyond its stated class.

statements.statement: For every \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)=\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}\). Static equality can be decided using \(O(p^3)\) elementary comparisons with adjacency matrices and canonical block bitsets. The enumeration is duplicate-free by exact state memoization, terminates after at most \(p!\) emitted states, and a breadth-first predecessor tree returns for every emitted \(D\) a shortest path of length \(\delta(C,D)\).
statements.justification: The population characterization is operational because the canonical background PDAG and unique partition lift yield exact-once enumeration with explicit delay, size, and certificate guarantees.
statements.gap: WienobstLuttermannBannachLiskiewicz2023 handles PDAG extensions but not target partitions; the local bijection proves output-linear lifting and eliminates state-dependent transport tests.
statements.consumer: Component enumeration supplies every graph-specific adjustment and path functional needed for possible-effect analysis, with optional shortest legal-reversal certificates.
statements.proof_tex:
The canonical-lift proposition \(\texttt{prop:canonical-pdag-component-lift}\) proves that the primary procedure in \(\texttt{def:component-enumerator}\) emits every state of \(\mathcal R(C)\) exactly once. The same proposition proves the legal-reversal breadth-first fallback has visited set \(\mathcal R(C)\). Therefore
\[
 \operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C).
\]
The equivalence theorem \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) then gives the observable static characterization
\[
 \operatorname{Enum}(C)=\mathcal R(C)
 =\{D\in\mathfrak S_p:\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\}.
\]

We spell out the static decision bound. With a \(p\)-by-\(p\) adjacency matrix, skeleton equality costs \(O(p^2)\) elementary comparisons. Enumerating ordered triples and testing whether two incoming adjacencies form an unshielded collider costs \(O(p^3)\). At each vertex, encode every block by a \(p\)-bit incidence vector and sort or index blocks by their least member. Because the blocks are disjoint, forming and comparing all canonical vertex-indexed nonsingleton families costs \(O(p^3)\) bit comparisons. Once those families are known, scanning the at most \(p(p-1)/2\) adjacencies compares the oriented family-mismatch sets in \(O(p^2)\). Thus equality of \(\mathsf S(C)\) and \(\mathsf S(D)\) is decided using \(O(p^3)\) elementary comparisons.

The canonical proposition also proves
\[
 |\operatorname{Enum}(C)|=|\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!,
\]
and shows the bound is attained by the complete all-singleton state. The cited PDAG algorithm makes the primary procedure exact-once. In the fallback, the state space is finite and a state is enqueued only on its first visit, so exact memoization both prevents duplicate emission and proves termination after at most \(p!\) outputs.

Finally, breadth-first search in an unweighted move graph records a minimum-length predecessor path. The distance statement in \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) identifies its length for every emitted \(D\) as
\[
 d_{\mathrm{rev}}(C,D)=\delta(C,D).
\]
This proves every assertion in the proposition. The stronger output-delay, canonical-lift, path-independence, and sharpness conclusions are recorded explicitly in \(\texttt{prop:canonical-pdag-component-lift}\).

statements.statement: If every block of \(C\) is a singleton, then \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\varnothing\) for all \(j\) and \(\mathcal R(C)\) is exactly the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of \(G\), with \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}=\delta\) as in Chickering1995. If no block of \(C\) is a singleton, then every edge is fixed and \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\) as in the BPEC identifiability boundary. If \(G=H\) and \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\), then \(\Pi=\Lambda\).
statements.justification: The two extreme partitions verify that the characterization interpolates exactly between ordinary Markov equivalence and proper blocked identifiability.
statements.gap: The two endpoint results are published separately by Chickering1995 and BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026; their exact interpolation within one full-model criterion is new.
statements.consumer: These reductions provide regression tests for software and prevent interpreting every fixed arrow as a numerically identified direct effect.
statements.proof_tex:
If every block of \(C\) is a singleton, then \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\varnothing\) for every \(j\), so \(F(C)=\varnothing\). The static criterion of \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) then reduces exactly to equality of skeleton and unshielded colliders. By \(\texttt{lem:verma-pearl-markov-equivalence}\), this is the ordinary Markov-equivalence class of \(G\), and the distance equality in the theorem gives \(d_{\mathrm{rev}}=\delta\).

If no block of \(C\) is a singleton, take any edge \(i\to j\). Its block \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) contains \(i\), while no block at \(i\) can contain \(i\). Hence \(\mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)\). Every edge therefore belongs to \(F(C)\) and its orientation is fixed by the static criterion. Once the graph is fixed, the fixed nonsingleton families give the whole partition because there is no singleton remainder. Thus \(\mathcal R(C)=\{C\}\), agreeing with the cited BPEC boundary.

Finally, if \(G=H\) and the models are equal, \(\texttt{lem:tangent-block-recovery}\) gives \(\mathcal N_j(C)=\mathcal N_j(D)\) at every vertex. Their parent sets are already identical. A partition is uniquely the displayed nonsingleton blocks together with singleton blocks for all remaining parents, so \(\Pi_j=\Lambda_j\) for every \(j\), and \(\Pi=\Lambda\).

statements.statement: Fix \(p\), \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), and a parameter \(\theta_C\in\Theta_C\setminus\mathcal E_C\) with \(\Sigma_0=\phi_C(\theta_C)\). For each integer \(n\geq p\), let \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) be independent \(N_p(0,\Sigma_0)\) observations and let \(\widehat C_n\) be the deterministically tie-broken global minimizer in \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\). Then \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) almost surely. Consequently every statewise block Gram matrix \(\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)\) is invertible, every constrained residual variance in \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\) is strictly positive, and only the finite attained likelihood branch is used. As \(n\to\infty\) through integers satisfying \(n\geq p\), \[\Pr\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\}\longrightarrow1.\] The exceptional set is proper algebraic: models of dimension at most \(d_C\) are excluded by their nonzero pulled-back defining polynomials, while larger models lose by the diverging dimension penalty. This is component recovery, not consistency of greedy GECS.
statements.justification: Singleton blocks change the estimable structural target from one state to an exact quotient component, so selection consistency must quotient identical covariance images.
statements.gap: BoegeKubjasMisraSolus2026, Section 6 and Discussion, derives a decomposable BIC and reports GECS simulations but leaves consistency open; Haughton1988 treats finitely many smooth models without the blocked-state equality quotient.
statements.consumer: A fixed-dimensional coloured-DAG analysis can consistently report the right component even when several singleton-block orientations have exactly equal likelihood.
statements.proof_tex:
Write \(d_E=p+\sum_j|\Pi^E_j|\). By \(\texttt{lem:blocked-model-geometry}\), \(\mathcal M(E)\) is a connected, relatively closed embedded submanifold of \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\) of dimension \(d_E\), described there by finitely many polynomial equalities after positive denominators are cleared.

We first justify properness of \(\mathcal E_C\). Fix \(D\) with \(d_D\leq d_C\) and \(\mathcal M(D)\neq\mathcal M(C)\). If \(d_D<d_C\), an embedded \(d_C\)-manifold cannot be contained in an embedded \(d_D\)-manifold. If \(d_D=d_C\) and \(\mathcal M(C)\subseteq\mathcal M(D)\), equal-dimensional manifold charts make the inclusion locally open, while relative closedness makes \(\mathcal M(C)\) closed in \(\mathcal M(D)\). Connectedness of \(\mathcal M(D)\) would then imply equality, a contradiction. Thus \(\mathcal M(C)\nsubseteq\mathcal M(D)\). At least one polynomial equality defining \(\mathcal M(D)\) consequently pulls back under \(\phi_C\) to a nonzero polynomial on \(\Theta_C\). Its zero set contains the relevant intersection pullback used in \(\texttt{def:generic-exception}\).

For a reported effect coordinate that is nonconstant on \(\mathcal M(C)\), its rational composition with \(\phi_C\) is nonconstant; hence its derivative is not identically zero. Clearing its positive Gram denominators shows that its zero-gradient locus is also contained in the zero set of a nonzero polynomial. There are only finitely many states and reported coordinates. The product of the resulting nonzero polynomials is nonzero, so its zero set cannot contain the open parameter domain \(\Theta_C\). Therefore \(\mathcal E_C\subsetneq\Theta_C\) is proper algebraic. Since \(\theta_C\notin\mathcal E_C\),
\[
 \Sigma_0\notin\mathcal M(D)
 \quad\text{for every nonequivalent }D\text{ with }d_D\leq d_C.
\]

By \(\texttt{lem:fixed-p-gaussian-covariance-calculus}\), \(S_n\) is positive definite almost surely for every \(n\geq p\). For nonempty \(P_{Ej}\), the block-incidence matrix has full column rank because its nonempty block columns have disjoint supports. Hence
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)u
 =(A_{Ej}u)^{\mathsf T}S_{n,P_{Ej}P_{Ej}}(A_{Ej}u)>0
\]
for every \(u\neq0\). The residual variance is the Schur complement after regression on the full-rank block-sum design and is strictly positive. Thus the likelihood branch in \(\texttt{def:global-bic}\) is finite and attained.

For completeness, compare the criteria directly. Up to a constant independent of \(\Sigma\),
\[
 \ell_n(\Sigma)=-\frac n2\{\log\det\Sigma+operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^{-1}S_n)\}.
\]
The population likelihood contrast is
\[
 K(\Sigma_0,\Sigma)=\frac12\left\{
 \operatorname{tr}(\Sigma^{-1}\Sigma_0)
 -\log\det(\Sigma^{-1}\Sigma_0)-p\right\}\geq0.
\]
Diagonalizing \(\Sigma^{-1/2}\Sigma_0\Sigma^{-1/2}\) reduces the inequality to \(u-\log u-1\geq0\), with equality only at \(u=1\); hence equality holds only for \(\Sigma=\Sigma_0\). Its sublevel sets are compact inside the positive-definite cone because the same scalar expression diverges when an eigenvalue tends to zero or infinity. Relative closedness of \(\mathcal M(D)\) and \(\Sigma_0\notin\mathcal M(D)\) therefore give
\[
 \kappa_D:=\inf_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(D)}K(\Sigma_0,\Sigma)>0
\]
for every nonequivalent \(D\) with \(d_D\leq d_C\). Since \(S_n\to\Sigma_0\) in probability, the sample contrast converges uniformly on each such compact sublevel set; outside one fixed sublevel set it is uniformly worse with probability tending one. Consequently
\[
 \sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(D)}\ell_n(\Sigma)
 -\sup_{\Sigma\in\mathcal M(C)}\ell_n(\Sigma)
 \leq-n\kappa_D+o_{\mathbb P}(n).
\]
The \(O(\log n)\) penalty difference cannot offset this loss.

If instead \(d_D>d_C\), let \(\ell_n(S_n)\) denote the saturated maximum. Because \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M(C)\),
\[
 \sup_{\mathcal M(D)}\ell_n-\sup_{\mathcal M(C)}\ell_n
 \leq \ell_n(S_n)-\ell_n(\Sigma_0).
\]
Writing \(S_n=\Sigma_0+\Delta_n\), the first-order terms in the Taylor expansion of the right-hand side cancel, and \(\sqrt n\Delta_n=O_{\mathbb P}(1)\) by \(\texttt{lem:fixed-p-gaussian-covariance-calculus}\). Hence
\[
 \ell_n(S_n)-\ell_n(\Sigma_0)=O_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
It follows that
\[
 \operatorname{BIC}_n(D)-\operatorname{BIC}_n(C)
 \geq(d_D-d_C)\log n-O_{\mathbb P}(1)\longrightarrow+\infty
\]
in probability.

The class \(\mathfrak S_p\) is finite, so with probability tending one every nonequivalent state loses to \(C\). Every remaining minimizer has covariance model \(\mathcal M(C)\); such states have dimension \(d_C\) because equal embedded images have equal dimension. The main equivalence theorem then yields \(\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\). The argument concerns the stated global minimizer only and makes no assertion about greedy search.

statements.statement: Under the conditions of \(\texttt{thm:generic-bic-component-recovery}\), fix finite \(\mathcal Q\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1)\). Along integers \(n\geq p\), the event \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) has probability one. Hence every \(L_E(S_n)\) is obtained from the uniquely solvable block-constrained Gram systems in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\), and every derivative \(\mathrm D g_E(S_n)\) is evaluated inside the positive-definite cone on which \(g_E\) is rational and smooth. Then \(\mathcal T_{\widehat C_n}(S_n)\) converges in probability to \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\) in Hausdorff distance. With \(\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\) defined memberwise before removing numerical duplicates, \[\liminf_{\substack{n\to\infty\\ n\geq p}}\Pr\left\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\text{ and }g_E(\Sigma_0)\text{ belongs to its labelled interval in }\mathfrak I_{n,\alpha}(\widehat C_n)\text{ for every }E\in\mathcal R(C)\right\}\geq1-\alpha.\] The conclusion permits coincident effect values and singular joint covariance because only marginal nonconstant-coordinate variances enter the Bonferroni construction.
statements.justification: The observationally identified object is a finite set of possible effects, so valid inference must cover all component members rather than one selected graph.
statements.gap: MaathuisKalischBuhlmann2009 proves consistency of possible-effect multisets without simultaneous intervals, while ChangGuoMalinsky2026 targets coverage of one fixed true effect after graph screening rather than every member of a full-model-equivalence effect set.
statements.consumer: An analyst using the Sachs protein network can report simultaneous uncertainty for every total effect compatible with the recovered coefficient-community component.
statements.proof_tex:
First connect the observable functionals to the causal target. If \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), the main theorem gives \(\mathcal M(E)=\mathcal M(C)\), so \(\Sigma_0\in\mathcal M(E)\). In the acyclic structural model for \(E\), the innovation at target \(j\) is independent of its parents. Therefore its population parent-regression coefficient is its structural coefficient row. The block-constrained normal equations in \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\) have a unique solution, so
\[
 L_E(\Sigma_0)=B_E.
\]
Under an intervention on coordinate \(a\), differentiating the acyclic structural equations with respect to the intervention level gives the path-sum vector \((I_p-B_E)^{-1}e_a\). Hence \(((I_p-B_E)^{-1})_{ya}\) is the total causal effect of \(a\) on \(y\). It follows that \(g_E(\Sigma_0)\) is the member-labelled causal-effect vector, and \(\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\) is the finite causal target rather than its estimator.

By \(\texttt{lem:fixed-p-gaussian-covariance-calculus}\), \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) almost surely for \(n\geq p\) and \(S_n\to\Sigma_0\) in probability. Positive definiteness and the full column rank of each block-incidence matrix make every \(\Gamma_{Ej}(S_n)\) positive definite, so the maps and derivatives in the statement are evaluated on their declared open domain.

Let \(A_n=\{\mathcal R(\widehat C_n)=\mathcal R(C)\}\). The BIC theorem gives \(\Pr(A_n)\to1\). On \(A_n\), the two components have the same finite index set and continuity of every rational \(g_E\) at \(\Sigma_0\) yields
\[
 d_H\{\mathcal T_{\widehat C_n}(S_n),\mathcal T_C(\Sigma_0)\}
 \leq\max_{E\in\mathcal R(C)}\|g_E(S_n)-g_E(\Sigma_0)\|\ \xrightarrow{\mathbb P}\ 0.
\]
Outside \(A_n\) the probability tends to zero, proving unconditional Hausdorff convergence in probability.

For simultaneous coverage, retain member labels even when numerical effect values coincide. Flatten the finitely many member and query coordinates. Coordinates that are identically zero are covered by their singleton intervals with probability one. For every remaining coordinate \(f=g_{E,k}\), the exclusion \(\theta_C\notin\mathcal E_C\) gives \(\mathrm Df(\Sigma_0)\neq0\). The covariance of Gaussian sample-covariance coordinates is
\[
 (V_0)_{ij,kl}=\Sigma_{0,ik}\Sigma_{0,jl}+\Sigma_{0,il}\Sigma_{0,jk}.
\]
It is positive definite on nonzero symmetric derivatives by \(\texttt{lem:fixed-p-gaussian-covariance-calculus}\). Thus each plug-in studentized error converges marginally to \(N(0,1)\). If \(K\geq1\) is the fixed number of these labelled nonconstant coordinates, each two-sided interval with critical value \(z_{1-\alpha/(2K)}\) has limiting noncoverage at most \(\alpha/K\). The union bound, which requires no nonsingularity of the stacked covariance, gives
\[
 \limsup_n\Pr\{\text{some labelled coordinate is not covered}\}\leq\alpha.
\]
When \(K=0\), all intervals are exact and the same assertion is immediate. Finally,
\[
 \Pr(A_n\cap\{\text{all labelled coordinates covered}\})
 \geq 1-\Pr(A_n^c)-\Pr\{\text{some coordinate is not covered}\},
\]
and taking the lower limit proves the displayed bound. Coincident member values do not change the labelled union bound, and a singular joint covariance is harmless because only the positive marginal variances are studentized.

statements.statement: Using \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{enum}}\), can one construct an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay algorithm that emits each distinct rational total-effect functional \(g_E\), for \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\), exactly once and returns a certificate partitioning all states by functional equality, while preserving the shortest legal-reversal certificates from \(C\)? The construction must derive path independence of transported partitions and may not assume that numerically coincident evaluations identify equal rational functionals.
statements.justification: After state enumeration is solved, the remaining computational bottleneck is exact output-sensitive quotienting by genuinely distinct rational causal-effect maps.
statements.gap: Neither PDAG enumeration nor known-graph effect estimation supplies deterministic polynomial-delay canonicalization of compact rational circuits under global identity.
statements.consumer: A solution would let large components feed possible-effect analysis with one certified output per distinct functional rather than one per state.

obligation.what_is_open: Whether equivalence classes of compact circuits for \(g_E\) under global rational identity on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\) can be enumerated deterministically in output-polynomial total time or polynomial delay, with an exact class certificate for every state.
obligation.obstruction: Clearing positive denominators reduces equality to multivariate polynomial identity. Expansion gives an exact deterministic certificate but may be exponential in compact circuit size, and the number of states may be exponentially larger than the number of distinct rational maps. The frozen core supplies no deterministic polynomial-time circuit canonical form or identity algorithm that removes both costs.
obligation.attempted: The canonical PDAG algorithm eliminated path-dependent partition transport and gives linear delay in state outputs. Rational maps were represented by exact arithmetic circuits, their positive denominators were cleared, and expanded coefficient tables were used to decide global identity exactly. This closes correctness but not delay measured in distinct functional outputs.
obligation.partial_result: The state side is closed. The canonical PDAG algorithm enumerates every \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\) exactly once after \(O(p^3)\) initialization and with \(O(p+m)\) delay, and the unique formula for \(\mathsf L_C(H)\) proves transported partitions are path independent. Shortest certificates of length \(\delta(C,E)\) can be produced with the safe per-output bound \(O(p^5)\). For the effect side, \(\texttt{lem:exact-global-rational-effect-identity}\) proves a terminating deterministic exact test: clear the positive Gram-determinant denominators and expand every resulting numerator polynomial, whose coefficient table certifies global identity on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\). Enumerating all states and applying this test yields an exact finite partition and one representative per rational-functional class. The expansion and all-state traversal can be exponential in compact circuit size or in the number of distinct functionals, so this is not an output-polynomial or polynomial-delay solution to the narrowed question.

statements.statement:
For every \(E\in\mathfrak S_p\), the map \(\phi_E:\Theta_E\to\mathbb S^p_{++}\) is an injective smooth embedding with connected, relatively closed image \(\mathcal M(E)\) of dimension \(p+\sum_{j\in V}|\Pi^E_j|\). At the identity, its differential satisfies
\[
 \operatorname{proj}_{\mathrm{off}}T_{I_p}\mathcal M(E)
 =\operatorname{span}\{v_{jB}:j\in V,\ B\in\Pi^E_j\},
 \qquad (v_{jB})_{\{i,j\}}=\mathbf 1\{i\in B\}.
\]
Moreover, \(\mathcal M(E)\) is the common zero set, inside \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), of finitely many rational equalities whose denominators are positive principal minors; after clearing those denominators the equalities are polynomial.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(E\). Acyclicity in \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\) gives a topological order. Hence \(B_E\) is nilpotent in that order and
\[
 (I_p-B_E)^{-1}=I_p+B_E+\cdots+B_E^{p-1}.
\]
Thus \(\phi_E\) is polynomial in \((\beta_E,\omega_E)\) and takes values in \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\), because \(\operatorname{diag}(\omega_E)\) is positive definite by \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\).

Let \(P_j=\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(j)\). In the structural equation
\[
 X_j=(B_E)_{jP_j}X_{P_j}+\varepsilon_j,
\]
every coordinate of \(X_{P_j}\) is a function only of innovations preceding \(j\) in a topological order. It is therefore independent of \(\varepsilon_j\). Consequently, for \(\Sigma=\phi_E(\beta_E,\omega_E)\),
\[
 (B_E)_{jP_j}=\Sigma_{jP_j}\Sigma_{P_jP_j}^{-1},
 \qquad
 \omega_{Ej}=\Sigma_{jj}-\Sigma_{jP_j}\Sigma_{P_jP_j}^{-1}\Sigma_{P_jj}.
\]
Every principal matrix \(\Sigma_{P_jP_j}\) is positive definite, including the empty case by the usual empty-matrix convention. These formulas give a rational smooth left inverse of \(\phi_E\) on its image. Thus \(\phi_E\) is injective, its differential is injective, and its inverse onto its image is continuous. It is therefore a smooth embedding. Its dimension is the dimension of \(\Theta_E\), namely \(p+\sum_j|\Pi^E_j|\), and its image is connected because \(\Theta_E=\mathbb R^{b_E}\times(0,\infty)^p\) is connected.

For relative closedness, for arbitrary \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) define the unrestricted parent-regression row
\[
 \widetilde B_{jP_j}(\Sigma)=\Sigma_{jP_j}\Sigma_{P_jP_j}^{-1},
 \qquad \widetilde B_{ji}(\Sigma)=0\quad(i\notin P_j).
\]
Then \(\Sigma\in\mathcal M(E)\) if and only if (i) \(\widetilde B_{ji}(\Sigma)=\widetilde B_{jk}(\Sigma)\) whenever \(i,k\) lie in the same block of \(\Pi^E_j\), and (ii)
\[
 (I_p-\widetilde B(\Sigma))\Sigma(I_p-\widetilde B(\Sigma))^{\mathsf T}
\]
is diagonal. Necessity follows from the recovered structural parameters above. Conversely, (i) assembles \(\widetilde B\) from a legal \(\beta_E\), while (ii) gives a diagonal innovation covariance; its diagonal is strictly positive because it is a congruence of \(\Sigma\) by the invertible acyclic matrix \(I_p-\widetilde B\). Hence the covariance formula in \(\texttt{def:covariance-model}\) holds. Conditions (i)--(ii) are finitely many continuous rational equalities on the positive-definite cone, so their common zero set is relatively closed. Their only denominators are determinants of positive-definite principal submatrices, which are positive; multiplying them out gives equivalent polynomial equalities.

Finally evaluate the differential at \(\beta_E=0\) and \(\omega_E=(1,\ldots,1)\), which maps to \(I_p\). Differentiating the covariance formula yields
\[
 d\Sigma=dB_E+dB_E^{\mathsf T}+\operatorname{diag}(d\omega_E).
\]
The derivative in the coordinate \(\beta_{jB}\) is one precisely on the unordered off-diagonal coordinates \(\{\{i,j\}:i\in B\}\), and the variance derivatives are diagonal. Projection off the diagonal gives the displayed tangent space. This also directly verifies the construction in \(\texttt{def:offdiagonal-tangent}\).

statements.statement: For blocked states \(C=(G,\Pi)\) and \(D=(H,\Lambda)\), equality \(\mathcal M(C)=\mathcal M(D)\) implies that \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent; in particular, they have the same skeleton and the same unshielded colliders.

source.verbatim_statement: Let \((G,c)\) and \((H,d)\) be model equivalent colored DAGs. Suppose that \(c\) is a vertex- (edge-) coloring and that \(d\) is a vertex- (edge-) coloring. Then \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent DAGs. Hence, they have the same skeleton and v-structures.

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2404.04024v3, Corollary 5.6 in the HTML version dated August 24, 2026.

statements.statement: Two directed acyclic graphs on the same labelled vertex set are Markov equivalent if and only if they have the same skeleton and the same unshielded colliders.

source.verbatim_statement: Two dags are equivalent if and only if they have the same skeletons and the same v-structures.

upstream.citation: Thomas Verma and Judea Pearl. Equivalence and Synthesis of Causal Models. Proceedings of the Sixth Conference on Uncertainty in Artificial Intelligence, 220--227, 1990.

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published-source scan at arXiv:1302.4938, page 88, where Chickering attributes the theorem to Verma and Pearl.

statements.statement: If the directed acyclic graphs \(G\) and \(H\) are Markov equivalent and \(\delta(C,D)\) of their common-skeleton edges have opposite orientations, then \(G\) can be transformed into \(H\) by exactly \(\delta(C,D)\) distinct covered-edge reversals. Every intermediate graph is acyclic and Markov equivalent to \(G\).

source.verbatim_statement: Let \(g\) and \(g'\) be any pair of dags such that \(g\) and \(g'\) are equivalent. There exists a sequence of \(|\Delta(g,g')|\) distinct edge reversals in \(g\) with the following properties: each edge reversed in \(g\) is a covered edge; after each reversal, \(g\) is a dag equivalent to \(g'\); and after all reversals, \(g=g'\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published-source scan at arXiv:1302.4938, Theorem 2, page 89; mathematical glyphs were normalized to LaTeX.

statements.statement: If \(E' = \operatorname{rev}_{i\to j}(E)\) is defined by \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\), then \(E'\in\mathfrak S_p\), the reverse transformation \(\operatorname{rev}_{j\to i}(E')\) is defined and equals \(E\), and \(\mathcal M(E')=\mathcal M(E)\). The nonsingleton families are preserved at every vertex.
statements.proof_tex:
Put \(S=\operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(i)\). Definedness of the move gives
\[
 \operatorname{pa}_{G_E}(j)=S\cup\{i\},\qquad
 \{i\}\in\Pi^E_j,\qquad
 \Pi^E_j\setminus\{\{i\}\}=\Pi^E_i.
\]
Reversing a covered edge preserves acyclicity: if reversal of \(i\to j\) created a directed cycle, the old graph would contain a directed path from \(i\) to \(j\) other than the edge. If \(k\to j\) is the last edge of a shortest such path, coveredness gives \(k\to i\), which together with the initial segment \(i\leadsto k\) is already a directed cycle in \(G_E\), a contradiction. The transported partitions in \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\) partition the new parent sets, so \(E'\in\mathfrak S_p\). They also show directly that the reverse move is defined and returns \(E\).

It remains to prove equality of covariance images, rather than merely ordinary Markov equivalence. Conditional on \(X_S\), write the two affected structural equations as
\[
 X_i=a^{\mathsf T}X_S+\varepsilon_i,\qquad
 X_j=bX_i+d^{\mathsf T}X_S+\varepsilon_j,
\]
where \(u=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_i)>0\), \(v=\operatorname{Var}(\varepsilon_j)>0\), and all innovations are mutually independent. Both \(a\) and \(d\) are constant on every block of the common partition \(\Pi^E_i\). Set
\[
 t=v+b^2u>0,\qquad q=\frac{bu}{t},\qquad
 \eta_j=b\varepsilon_i+\varepsilon_j,\qquad
 \eta_i=\varepsilon_i-q\eta_j.
\]
Direct substitution gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 X_j&=(d+ba)^{\mathsf T}X_S+\eta_j,\\
 X_i&=qX_j+\{a-q(d+ba)\}^{\mathsf T}X_S+\eta_i.
 \end{aligned}
\]
Furthermore,
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(\eta_j)=t,\qquad
 \operatorname{Var}(\eta_i)=\frac{uv}{t}>0,\qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(\eta_i,\eta_j)=bu-qt=0.
\]
The pair \((\eta_i,\eta_j)\) is jointly Gaussian, so zero covariance implies independence; being a linear transformation of \((\varepsilon_i,\varepsilon_j)\), it is also independent of every other innovation. Both new coefficient vectors \(d+ba\) and \(a-q(d+ba)\) remain constant on every common block, while the reversed coefficient \(q\) occupies the transported singleton \(\{j\}\). Thus every covariance in \(\mathcal M(E)\) lies in \(\mathcal M(E')\). Applying the same construction to the inverse legal move gives the reverse inclusion.

Finally, \(\Pi^{E'}_j=\Pi^E_i\) and \(\Pi^{E'}_i=\Pi^E_i\cup\{\{j\}\}\); hence their nonsingleton subfamilies equal the common nonsingleton family of \(i\) and \(j\), and all other partitions are unchanged. Therefore every \(\mathcal N_k\) is preserved.

statements.statement: Within the BPEC class of properly blocked edge-coloured directed acyclic graphs, equality of covariance models identifies the entire edge-coloured directed acyclic graph.

source.verbatim_statement: Let \([G,c]\) be the model equivalence class of a BPEC-DAG \((G,c)\). Then \(|\mathcal{BP}\cap[G,c]|=1\); i.e., an edge-colored DAG is structurally identifiable in the set of BPEC-DAGs.

attestation.note: Transcribed from arXiv:2404.04024v3, Theorem 5.17 in the HTML version dated August 24, 2026.

statements.statement:
Fix \(p\) and let \(X^{(1)},\ldots,X^{(n)}\) be independent \(N_p(0,\Sigma_0)\) vectors with \(\Sigma_0\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\). If \(n\geq p\), then \(S_n\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\) almost surely. Let \(\operatorname{vech}\) stack the upper-triangular entries of a symmetric matrix, and let \(V_0\) be indexed by unordered pairs with entries \((V_0)_{ij,kl}=\Sigma_{0,ik}\Sigma_{0,jl}+\Sigma_{0,il}\Sigma_{0,jk}\). Then \(S_n\to\Sigma_0\) in \(L^2\), and
\[
 \sqrt n\,\operatorname{vech}(S_n-\Sigma_0)\ \Longrightarrow\ N(0,V_0),
 \qquad
 \operatorname{Cov}(X_iX_j,X_kX_l)=(V_0)_{ij,kl}.
\]
The covariance \(V_0\) is positive definite on nonzero symmetric directions. Consequently every continuously differentiable scalar functional with nonzero derivative at \(\Sigma_0\) obeys the corresponding studentized plug-in delta limit.
statements.proof_tex:
Let \(Z\) be the \(p\)-by-\(n\) matrix with columns \(\Sigma_0^{-1/2}X^{(r)}\). Its entries have a joint density. When \(n\geq p\), the set on which every \(p\)-by-\(p\) minor vanishes is the zero set of nonzero polynomials and has Lebesgue measure zero. Thus \(Z\), and hence the data matrix, has row rank \(p\) almost surely. Therefore \(S_n=n^{-1}XX^{\mathsf T}\) is positive definite almost surely.

Differentiating the Gaussian moment-generating function \(\exp(t^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_0t/2)\) four times at zero gives
\[
 \mathbb E[X_iX_jX_kX_l]
 =\Sigma_{0,ij}\Sigma_{0,kl}+\Sigma_{0,ik}\Sigma_{0,jl}+\Sigma_{0,il}\Sigma_{0,jk}.
\]
It follows that the displayed covariance formula holds and that
\(\mathbb E\|S_n-\Sigma_0\|_F^2=O(n^{-1})\), proving \(L^2\) convergence.

For the limit law, put \(W_r=\operatorname{vech}(X^{(r)}X^{(r)\mathsf T}-\Sigma_0)\). These vectors are independent, centered, have covariance \(V_0\), and have finite third moments. For each fixed vector \(t\), Taylor's formula for the characteristic function, with the cubic remainder bounded by the finite third moment, gives
\[
 \mathbb E\exp\{i t^{\mathsf T}W_1/\sqrt n\}
 =1-\frac{t^{\mathsf T}V_0t}{2n}+O(n^{-3/2}).
\]
Taking the \(n\)-th power yields \(\exp(-t^{\mathsf T}V_0t/2)\), the characteristic function of \(N(0,V_0)\), which proves the stated convergence.

If \(A\neq0\) is symmetric, then the corresponding quadratic-form direction has variance
\[
 \operatorname{Var}(X^{\mathsf T}AX)=2\operatorname{tr}\{(\Sigma_0^{1/2}A\Sigma_0^{1/2})^2\}>0.
\]
Thus \(V_0\) is positive definite on symmetric coordinates. If \(f\) is continuously differentiable at \(\Sigma_0\), Taylor expansion gives
\[
 \sqrt n\{f(S_n)-f(\Sigma_0)\}
 =\mathrm Df(\Sigma_0)[\sqrt n(S_n-\Sigma_0)]+o_{\mathbb P}(1).
\]
The preceding characteristic-function limit gives the normal law. Replacing \(\Sigma_0\) in the polynomial covariance formula by \(S_n\) is consistent by \(S_n\to\Sigma_0\), so division by the plug-in standard error gives a standard normal limit whenever \(\mathrm Df(\Sigma_0)\neq0\).

statements.statement: For a partially directed acyclic graph on \(p\) vertices and \(m\) edges, there is an algorithm that enumerates every consistent directed-acyclic extension exactly once after \(O(p^3)\) initialization, with \(O(p+m)\) worst-case delay.

source.verbatim_statement: There is an algorithm that enumerates all consistent extensions of a given PDAG with linear-time delay after an initialization step of time \(O(n^{3})\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the source-of-record arXiv HTML for Theorem 5; Algorithm 7 supplies exact consistent-extension enumeration, and the paper's linear-delay analysis is O(vertices plus edges).

statements.justification: This published algorithm supplies only the extension-enumeration complexity used after the local canonical-lift theorem.
statements.gap: The cited theorem enumerates PDAG extensions but has no coefficient-block state or partition-lift statement.
statements.consumer: The canonical-lift proposition transfers the algorithm to blocked covariance-equivalence components.

statements.statement: Fix \(C\in\mathfrak S_p\), let \(\mathcal P_C\) be the canonical background PDAG in \(\texttt{def:canonical-background-pdag}\), and let \(m=|\operatorname{skel}(G)|\). For every \(B\in\mathcal N_j(C)\) and \(i\in B\), \(\mathcal N_i(C)\neq\mathcal N_j(C)\) and \(i\to j\in F(C)\). Consequently every consistent DAG extension \(H\) of \(\mathcal P_C\) is in the domain of the canonical lift \(\mathsf L_C\), and \(H\mapsto\mathsf L_C(H)\) is a bijection from the consistent extensions of \(\mathcal P_C\) onto \(\mathcal R(C)\). The lift is therefore path independent. The canonical procedure in \(\operatorname{Enum}(C)\) emits every component state exactly once after \(O(p^3)\) initialization and with \(O(p+m)\) worst-case delay, including output-linear partition lifting. If a shortest legal-reversal certificate from \(C\) is emitted with each state, a direct covered-edge scan gives the safe bound \(O(p^5)\) per output and returns exactly \(\delta(C,D)\) legal reversals for output \(D\). Moreover, \(|\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!\), and this bound is sharp for the complete-skeleton all-singleton state. The legal-reversal breadth-first search remains a complete fallback and returns the same shortest certificates.
statements.proof_tex:
For \(j\in V\), abbreviate
\[
 \mathcal N_j=\mathcal N_j(C),
 \qquad
 U_j=\bigcup_{B\in\mathcal N_j}B.
\]
If \(B\in\mathcal N_j\) and \(i\in B\), then \(i\to j\) is an edge of \(G\). If \(\mathcal N_i=\mathcal N_j\), then \(B\in\mathcal N_i\). Every block in \(\mathcal N_i\) is contained in \(\operatorname{pa}_G(i)\), while \(i\in B\); this would be a self-loop at \(i\), contradicting acyclicity from \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\). Therefore
\[
 \mathcal N_i\neq\mathcal N_j,
 \qquad
 i\to j\in F(C)
\]
by \(\texttt{def:family-mismatch-edges}\).

The ordinary CPDAG of \(G\) represents exactly the DAGs Markov equivalent to \(G\). The PDAG \(\mathcal P_C\) additionally orients each arrow in \(F(C)\) as in \(G\). It has at least one consistent extension, namely \(G\), so the background knowledge is compatible. Let \(H\) be any consistent DAG extension of \(\mathcal P_C\). For every \(B\in\mathcal N_j\), the preceding display places every arrow \(i\to j\), \(i\in B\), in \(F(C)\), and \(H\) respects those background arrows. Hence
\[
 U_j\subseteq\operatorname{pa}_H(j).
\]
The blocks in \(\mathcal N_j\) are pairwise disjoint because they came from the partition \(\Pi_j\). Thus
\[
 \Lambda^H_j
 =\mathcal N_j\cup
   \left\{\{i\}:i\in\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\setminus U_j\right\}
\]
is a partition of \(\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\). Since \(H\) is acyclic, \(\mathsf L_C(H)=(H,\Lambda^H)\) belongs to \(\mathfrak S_p\) by \(\texttt{def:blocked-state-class}\), and its nonsingleton family at \(j\) is exactly \(\mathcal N_j\).

A consistent extension of \(\mathcal P_C\) has the skeleton and unshielded colliders of \(G\) and respects every orientation in \(F(C)\). Hence, using the displayed equality of nonsingleton families,
\[
 \mathsf S(\mathsf L_C(H))=\mathsf S(C).
\]
The equivalence theorem \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) gives
\[
 \mathsf L_C(H)\in\mathcal R(C).
\]

Conversely, take \(D=(H,\Lambda)\in\mathcal R(C)\). The same theorem gives \(\mathsf S(D)=\mathsf S(C)\). Thus \(H\) is Markov equivalent to \(G\), respects every arrow of \(F(C)\), and is a consistent extension of \(\mathcal P_C\). At vertex \(j\), the common nonsingleton family is \(\mathcal N_j\), and every parent outside \(U_j\) must be a singleton block. Therefore
\[
 \Lambda_j=\mathcal N_j\cup
 \left\{\{i\}:i\in\operatorname{pa}_H(j)\setminus U_j\right\}
 =\Lambda^H_j.
\]
So \(D=\mathsf L_C(H)\). The lift is injective because its graph coordinate is \(H\), and the two preceding directions prove surjectivity. This establishes the bijection and also path independence: the formula depends only on the endpoint parent sets and the fixed families, not on a path of reversals.

Apply the cited result \(\texttt{lem:pdag-consistent-extension-enumeration}\) to \(\mathcal P_C\). It computes the equivalent Meek-closed MPDAG during an \(O(p^3)\) initialization and emits every consistent extension once with delay \(O(p+m)\). The lift reuses the fixed blocks \(\mathcal N_j\) and scans each output DAG's \(p\) vertices and \(m\) edges once to append singleton remainder blocks. Its time and representation size are \(O(p+m)\), so composing enumeration with the bijection preserves \(O(p+m)\) delay and exact-once output; the primary procedure needs no state memoization.

For a shortest certificate to an emitted \(D=(H,\Lambda)\), start at \(G\). At a current DAG \(K\neq H\), \(\texttt{lem:chickering-monotone-covered-reversals}\), applied to \(K,H\), guarantees a covered edge whose orientation disagrees with \(H\). Scan the at most \(m\) disagreeing edges and compare the two parent-incidence rows, at cost \(O(mp)=O(p^3)\), until such an edge is found. Reverse it and repeat. Every reversal reduces the disagreement count by one, so there are exactly
\[
 \delta(C,D)\leq m=O(p^2)
\]
iterations and the crude total bound is \(O(m^2p)=O(p^5)\). Both endpoint DAGs respect \(F(C)\), so an edge of \(F(C)\) never disagrees and is never reversed. The legality argument in \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) therefore lifts every covered reversal through \(\mathsf L_C\); the resulting state path has length \(\delta(C,D)\), which that theorem proves is shortest. Generating this certificate for each graph output changes the delay to at most \(O(p^5)\), a safe polynomial bound.

For the cardinality bound, assign to each DAG in the component its lexicographically first topological order. A fixed skeleton together with a topological order determines every arrow: each adjacency points from its earlier endpoint to its later endpoint. Hence two component DAGs assigned the same order are equal. The canonical-lift bijection gives at most one state per such DAG, and there are \(p!\) total orders, so
\[
 |\mathcal R(C)|\leq p!.
\]
To see sharpness, take the complete skeleton and make every parent block a singleton. For each of the \(p!\) total orders, orient every complete-skeleton edge from the earlier to the later endpoint. These are distinct acyclic transitive tournaments. A complete skeleton has no unshielded collider, and in the all-singleton case \(\mathcal N_j=\varnothing\) and \(F(C)=\varnothing\) for every \(j\). All \(p!\) states therefore have the same static signature and belong to \(\mathcal R(C)\) by the equivalence theorem. Thus equality is attained.

Finally, the fallback breadth-first traversal applies precisely the reversible legal moves of \(\texttt{def:legal-reversal}\). Its exact visited set is the connected component \(\mathcal R(C)\) by \(\texttt{def:reversal-component}\), and exact memoization prevents duplicates and forces termination. Breadth-first predecessors minimize the number of moves; \(\texttt{thm:complete-blocked-equivalence}\) identifies that minimum as \(\delta(C,D)\). Hence the fallback returns the same component and shortest certificate lengths.
statements.justification: The static equivalence criterion becomes an exact output-sensitive state enumerator only after consistent graph extensions are shown to possess one canonical partition lift.
statements.gap: The cited PDAG algorithm has no partition data; the local proof supplies the lift, legal shortest certificates, and the sharp blocked-component bound.
statements.consumer: Component software can enumerate blocked states without testing path-dependent partition transports.

statements.statement: For any \(E,E'\in\mathcal R(C)\), equality \(g_E=g_{E'}\) as rational maps on \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\) is decidable by a deterministic exact finite procedure: write each coordinate over products of its positive block-Gram determinants, cross-multiply, and test whether every coefficient of each resulting numerator polynomial is zero. The expanded coefficient tables are exact identity certificates; agreement at finitely many numerical covariance matrices is not such a certificate.
statements.proof_tex:
Fix \(E\in\mathcal R(C)\) and \(\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}\). For every nonempty parent set, \(\texttt{def:off-model-block-ls}\) gives
\[
 \beta_{Ej}(\Sigma)
 =\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)^{-1}h_{Ej}(\Sigma)
 =\frac{\operatorname{adj}(\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma))h_{Ej}(\Sigma)}
        {\det\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)}.
\]
The block-incidence matrix has full column rank and \(\Sigma_{P_{Ej},P_{Ej}}\) is positive definite, so for every nonzero \(u\),
\[
 u^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)u
 =(A_{Ej}u)^{\mathsf T}\Sigma_{P_{Ej},P_{Ej}}(A_{Ej}u)>0.
\]
Hence every denominator \(\det\Gamma_{Ej}(\Sigma)\) is strictly positive throughout \(\mathbb S^p_{++}\). The entries of the adjugate and of \(h_{Ej}\) are polynomial in the entries of \(\Sigma\), so every entry of \(L_E(\Sigma)\) is rational with a product of these positive determinants as a possible common denominator.

Because the support of \(L_E(\Sigma)\) is the DAG \(G_E\), a topological permutation makes it strictly triangular. Therefore \(L_E(\Sigma)^p=0\) and
\[
 (I_p-L_E(\Sigma))^{-1}
 =I_p+L_E(\Sigma)+\cdots+L_E(\Sigma)^{p-1}.
\]
By \(\texttt{def:component-effect-set}\), every coordinate of \(g_E\) is consequently a rational function whose denominator is a product of positive block-Gram determinants. The same statements hold for \(E'\).

For one coordinate, put the difference over a common denominator:
\[
 g_{E,k}(\Sigma)-g_{E',k}(\Sigma)=\frac{N_k(\Sigma)}{Q_k(\Sigma)},
 \qquad Q_k(\Sigma)>0\quad\text{on }\mathbb S^p_{++},
\]
where \(N_k\) and \(Q_k\) are polynomials in the \(p(p+1)/2\) free symmetric entries. Thus the coordinate maps agree on the positive-definite cone exactly when \(N_k\) vanishes there. That cone is nonempty and open in \(\mathbb R^{p(p+1)/2}\). A real polynomial vanishing on a nonempty open set is the zero polynomial: for one variable this follows because a nonzero polynomial has only finitely many roots; induction on the number of variables follows by fixing all but one variable in an open box and applying the one-variable fact to each coefficient polynomial. Hence
\[
 N_k(\Sigma)=0\text{ for every }\Sigma\in\mathbb S^p_{++}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{every coefficient of }N_k\text{ is zero}.
\]
There are finitely many reported coordinates. Symbolic adjugation, multiplication, cross-multiplication, and expansion therefore give a terminating deterministic procedure, and the resulting coefficient tables certify equality or exhibit a nonzero coefficient certifying inequality. This proof supplies no polynomial bound in the compact input-circuit size; finite numerical agreement cannot replace the coefficient test.
statements.justification: The residual effect-enumeration question needs an exact equality notion and certificate before its complexity can be posed honestly.
statements.gap: Numerical coincidence is not rational identity, while compact-circuit canonicalization complexity is not supplied by the state-enumeration literature.
statements.consumer: A finite exact postprocessor can partition all enumerated states by global equality of their total-effect maps.
